topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: Rain slicks the streets, same as it does my mood. Found out today the tree I planted when I was a kid, barely more than a sapling holding onto the promise of summer, is nothing more than a memory. The stump's there, mocking me with its silence. It was supposed to grow, to stand the test of time, like a stubborn oath. Guess oaths are easier broken than a saw cutting through wood. Doesn’t matter how many times I circle the spot, it’s just not there. The neighborhood’s different now, people move, things change. But a damn tree, one I put my hands in the dirt for, should’ve been sacred. Just another thing that’s gone, leaving me standing in the rain, staring at a hole in the ground where a piece of my past used to be.
